issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a method addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int and a String reason), but the solution implementation provides addGuestStudents(int) with only the integer parameter. This parameter mismatch means the solution does not match the specified API and would confuse students about the expected method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the implementation signature match the specification: implement public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) in Lecture. Use the reason parameter as appropriate (e.g., log or store it), or if the reason is intentionally unnecessary, update the problem statement and UML to remove the String parameter so all artifacts agree.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML require an addGuestStudents(int, String) method (an int for the number of new guest students plus a String reason), and the template instructs students to implement that signature. The solution implementation instead provides addGuestStudents(int) with a single int parameter (named numberOfNewGuestStudents). This signature mismatch (missing String reason parameter) breaks the conceptual mapping between the exercise requirements and the provided solution, likely confusing students about the expected method signature and causing tests or examples that expect the reason parameter to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution implementation match the problem/UML signature by changing the solution method to accept the String reason parameter as specified. For example: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) { this.numberOfGuestStudents += numberOfNewGuestStudents; /* optionally record or log reason */ } Alternatively, if the reason parameter is intentionally unused, update the solution to include the parameter (and possibly document that it is currently unused) so the signature matches the exercise and template guidance.
